title: Pluggable driver API & dependency upgrades to stabilize load scheduler
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: The current load harness couples transport (gRPC) assumptions into the scenario driver and scheduler. That coupling blocks fast iteration on new async runners (HTTP/asyncio), makes dependency upgrades risky (grpcio pinned transitively), and contributes to occasional long-tail stalls under synthetic peak load. Goal: introduce a small pluggable driver API that isolates transport and runner semantics from scheduling logic, upgrade a set of core dependencies to the latest compatible versions, and fix a memory-growth regression observed in high-concurrency regression runs. Outcome should be a stable load scheduler that supports multiple driver implementations, allows incremental rollout, and reduces 95/99th latency variance by at least 20%.
proposal: Add Driver interface (Driver.start/stop/send_batch/metrics) with a minimal async contract and compatibility shim for the legacy blocking gRPC client.
Refactor scheduler to use the Driver interface; keep the previous scheduling algorithm intact during migration to minimize behavioral change.
Implement two drivers: grpc_compat (shim around existing sync client using thread pool) and http_async (aiohttp-based, non-blocking).
Upgrade pinned dependencies: grpcio -> 1.52.x, aiohttp -> 3.9.x, fasteners -> 0.18.x, protobuf -> 4.23.x. Run compatibility matrix checks for our models and runtime stubs.
Add e2e regression tests exercising both drivers under identical scenario specs and deterministic seeding.
Add CI job to run smoke load with the http_async driver on Merge to main and nightly perf regression comparisons.
Add runtime telemetry for per-driver latency histograms and bucketed memory summaries for quicker postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler uses Driver interface exclusively and legacy sync client is behind grpc_compat shim.
http_async driver passes full regression suite (load correctness, token accounting) in CI under 2k concurrent virtual users.
Dependency upgrades have no failing unit/integration tests and security scanners report zero critical findings.
Nightly perf regressions show a >=20% reduction in 99th percentile latency variance compared to baseline (prior month).
Memory growth under sustained synthetic load is eliminated for runs longer than 60 minutes in the staging harness.
Documentation updated: driver API spec, migration notes for integrators, and example configs for selecting driver per scenario.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (branch): implement Driver API + grpc_compat shim; run unit tests locally and open draft PR.
Phase 2 (canary): merge with feature flag defaulting to legacy path; enable http_async driver on staging scenarios behind opt-in flag.
Phase 3 (verify): run 48h smoking load with both drivers on staging, collect telemetry and perf diffs; adjust threadpool sizing and batching knobs.
Phase 4 (gradual): enable http_async as default for new scenarios and non-mission-critical customers; keep grpc_compat flag for enterprise builds for 2 weeks.
Phase 5 (cleanup): remove temporary shims and old sync-only client code after stability window and notify infra teams of dependency upgrades.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Upgrading grpcio/protobuf could change serialization behavior. Mitigation: run dedicated serialization compatibility tests with current model stubs and add protobuf round-trip tests.

Risk: http_async driver may expose previously unseen race under very high concurrency. Mitigation: run stress tests with deterministic seeds at 2x target concurrency and add additional backpressure (bounded queues) in driver implementation.
Risk: Nightly regressions may become noisy due to environment variability. Mitigation: pin staging node types for runs and use synthetic deterministic corpus to reduce noise.

Risk: Rollout impacts enterprise customers relying on the sync client. Mitigation: keep grpc_compat shim and a feature flag for at least two release cycles and coordinate with Customer Success for notifications.
